 Order

This revision petition is preferred by accused aggrieved by the rjejection of application under section 239 of Cr.P.C. by Addl. Civil Judge and JMFC., Court, Hosapete in CC No.697/2014 dated 06.09.2019.
2.
Though the case is listed for admission, with the consent of both parties matter is taken up for final disposal.

3. Brief facts leading to the filing of this petition is as under:
3.1. A private complaint came to be filed by the Regional Manager, Karnataka State Warehousing Corporation, Raichur against the petitioner herein.
It is the case of complainant that petitioner is working as Assistant Manager, Karnataka State Warehousing Corporation, Hosapete branch, Hosapet.
As per the order of the central office under Government scheme 7514.595 metric tones of Maize were purchased and sent to branch office at Hosapet where accused was working.

After 18 months 79,101 bags measuring 6444.820 Metric Tonnes of Maize were shown have been released thereby showing a shortage of 1069.775 metric tones, value of the same being Rs.89,86,110/-, leading to shortage and loss sustained by the Karnataka State Warehousing Corporation.

It is the case of complainant that petitioner being the officer in charge of godown was liable to maintenance of goods in good and proper condition by giving necessary protection to the goods from insecticides by taking precautions and keeping necessary medicine and was to maintain proper accounts and measurements of the goods supplied from time to time.
4. Petitioner had failed to discharge his duties thereby causing financial loss to the corporation.

Based on the complaint, FIR came to be registered in Crime No.67/2012 and investigation was undertaken and after completion of investigation, respondent-Police filed a charge sheet against petitioner for the offence punishable under Sections 119, 166, 409 and 420 of IPC.
According to prosecution, on the basis of statements of CWs.2 and 3, the auditor who conducted audit of records of godown furnished a report stating that there is a shortage of maize bags.
On 10.08.2010 as per the audit, maize kept in five godowns, the total weight measured 6444.820 metric tones instead of 7514.595 metric tones.
Therefore, there was shortage of 1069.775 metric tones amounting to Rs.89,86,110/- and as per the audit report, there was mis-appropriation of maize by petitioner.

After cognizance was taken petitioner-accused filed an application for discharge under Section 239 of Cr.P.C. stating that there were no grounds made out by the prosecution to frame charge against petitioner and accordingly sought for discharge of petitioner from the case.

sentences.text: 5. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Government Pleader for respondent- State.

6. It is the contention of learned counsel for petitioner that the trial Court has mis-directed itself and has committed gross illegality in not considering the fact that no materials were placed by the prosecution to frame charges against petitioner.

It is also contended by the learned counsel that there is no element of 'mens rea' to attract the offence alleged by prosecution and on the plain reading of the complaint, no offence is made out by prosecution and there are no grounds to proceed against the petitioner.

7. It is further contended that the trial Court has not applied it's mind while considering the reports of CW.2 and CW.3 who are the auditors and who have filed the reports which does not prima facie show that petitioner had mis- appropriated or mis-used the goods in his custody to cause loss to the State-exchequer.

It is the specific contention of learned counsel for petitioner that petitioner had communicated to the Managing Director and Regional Directors with regard to the deterioration of goods through his letter dated 03.12.2010, 09.05.2011 and 16.07.2011 and informed about the loss of goods well in advance.
This fact of the matter has been ignored by the Investigating Officer as well as the Court below.

It is his further contention that petitioner has taken reasonable care and precaution to preserve the goods despite which it has resulted in shortage which is beyond the control of petitioner and thereby he is not liable in view of Section 17 of Karnataka State Warehousing Corporation Act, 1961.
It is his further contention that the prosecution has not taken sanction to prosecute petitioner.
8. Learned counsel for the petitioner also contends that under the Karnataka State Warehousing Corporation Act, there was a specific provisions provided with regard to violation, breach and penalty.
It is his contention that prosecution has not lodged any case under the said Act.

Therefore,
when there is a special enactment, the present case filed is illegal and is not maintainable.
Under this ground also he is liable to be discharged.

Learned counsel for the petitioner relies on the judgment of Anand Ramdhani Chourasia and Another vs. The State of Maharastra and Others,
decided by Bombay High Court in WP No.3607/19(J) decided on 13.09.2019 and in the case of Ganesh Pandurang Jadhao and others vs. State of Maharastra and Others, reported in 2016 CRI.L.J.2401.

sentences.text: Therefore, on these grounds he seeks for allowing the revision petition and to set aside the order passed by trial Court.
9. Per contra, learned Government Pleader contends that the order passed by trial Court is in accordance with law and it does not warrant interference from the hands of this Court.

He further contends that on the basis of private complaint lodged by complainant, who himself is a Government servant against the petitioner for the loss caused to the State, the case came to be registered and after conducting proper investigation through audit report and other materials placed before the Court, charge sheet has been filed implicating the petitioner herein for the aforesaid offence.

It is further contended that admittedly, there is a shortage of maize which is borne by records submitted by auditors CW.2 and CW.3 and the Investigating Officer has drawn panchnama and recovered respecting trip sheets through which maize bags were transported and it is also not in dispute that petitioner is in-charge of Karnataka State Warehousing Corporation with Sri.Y.C.Basavaraj S/O. Late Channappa vs The State Of Karnataka on 22 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137257297/
3 regard to those godowns where the shortage of maize has occurred.

He further contends that when investigating authority has placed material before the Courts and has examined several witnesses and the audit report having been filed to show that there is shortage of Maize bags leading to shortage of loss of State exchequer to the tune of Rs.89,86,110/- which has been misappropriated by petitioner, it is the duty of petitioner to show that despite production of the materials before the Court, there is no ground made out for proceeding against petitioner.

Learned Government Pleader submits that petitioner has not placed any material or shown before this Court that there are no sufficient materials placed by the prosecution to frame charge against petitioner.

10. Having heard the learned counsel for petitioner and learned Government Pleader, the points that arise for consideration before this Court are 1) Whether the trial Court has committed any illegality or perversity in rejecting the application filed by petitioner for discharge under Section 239 of Cr.P.C? and 2) Whether interference is called for by this Court?

11. On perusal of the records, it is noticed that complaint has been registered by the Regional Manager, Karnataka State Warehouse Corporation against petitioner herein for misappropriation of maize to an extent of 1069.775 metric tones amounting to Rs.89,86,110/- which has lead to loss to the state exchequer.
After enquiry and investigation, charge sheet has been filed implicating petitioner herein for the offence punishable under Sections 119, 166, 409 and 420 of I.P.C.

It is the case of prosecution that, CWs.2 and 3 the Auditors have submitted a report showing a shortage of maize bags to the tune of 1069.775 metric tones, shortage was 14.23% of the total purchase of maize bags.
It is not in dispute that the petitioner herein has employed and working as Assistant Manager of Karnataka State Warehousing Corporation.
Further, it is not in dispute that the petitioner was in-charge of five godowns and where purchased maize bags were stored in the said branch of the said godown.
It is also not in dispute that the petitioner was entrusted with the 14.745 bags.
Pursuant to the investigation conducted by prosecution, prima- facie material was made out by the Investigating Officer by submitting the charge sheet against the petitioner.

12. It is during this time that petitioner filed the present application seeking for discharge on the premise that no valid grounds exist to proceed against petitioner and therefore he sought for discharge.
This Court consciously does not want to go into the merits and demerits of the matter.
Petitioner is exercising his option before this court in the revision jurisdiction.

This Court cannot sit in appeal to appreciate the evidentiary value or to find out inconsistencies in the statements of the witnesses and the lacuna created by the investigating agency, if any, while considering the application under Section 239 of Cr.P.C. for discharge of the petitioner/accused.
Trial Court has got limited and narrow powers to see where prima-facie case is made out by petitioner/accused to discharge due to unavailability of any ground to proceed against the petitioner.

In catena of decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court, it has been clearly laid down as to the manner in which the application for discharge has to be considered by trial Court and the test to be applied while considering such application.

In the present case on hand, according to the prosecution, there is material available on record and they have placed the same and it is a admitted fact that there is a Sri.Y.C.Basavaraj S/O. sentences.text: Hence, the application for discharge came to be rejected by trial Court.

13. The learned counsel for the petitioner has relied on two Judgments of Anand Ramdhani Chourasia and Another vs. The State of Maharastra and Others W.P.No.3607/2019, disposed off on 13.09.2019 of Bombay High Court and Ganesh Pandurang Jadhao and v. State of Maharastra and Others, reported in 2016 CRI.L.J.2401 also of Bombay High Court, both these cases pertain to the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

entities.text: Anand Ramdhani Chourasia and Another vs. The State of Maharastra and Others W.P.No.3607/2019,
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Ganesh Pandurang Jadhao and v. State of Maharastra and Others, reported in 2016 CRI.L.J.2401 also
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have gone through the Judgments relied by the learned counsel, the said Judgments are not applicable to present facts of the case.
Infact the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that there is no bar to trial or conviction under two different enactments.
14. In the present case, prosecution has initiated the action under Indian Penal Code and not under the Karnataka Warehousing Act, 1961.

The test for deciding the application under Section 239 of Cr.P.C. is that when there is a prima-facie case made out for proceeding against accused, charges shall be framed and while the considering the application under Section 239 of Cr.P.C, trial Court need not appreciate evidence and also need not find out inconsistencies in the statements of witnesses.

Even before this Court, it is to be kept in mind, this Court is exercising its revisional jurisdiction and not appellate jurisdiction to reconsider and reevaluate material evidence placed before the Court.

Therefore, while considering application for discharge, this Court need not look in the material evidence and inconsistencies pointed out by petitioner/accused and merely because the petitioner has preferred an application for discharge, this Court cannot become an appellate Court and start appreciating evidence or find out the inconsistencies in the statements of witnesses or the inconsistencies or lacuna of the investigation.

Therefore, on going through the material placed before this Court and the orders passed by the trial Court, there is no prima-facie case made out for discharge of the petitioner/accused at this stage of trial.

The petitioner will have to stand for trial on merits of the matter in the light of documents and contents of charge sheet laid by the respondent- State and trial Court has rightfully rejected the application for discharge thereby allowing the prosecution to prove its case on the materials placed before the Court.

15. Petitioner has not placed any material before this Court to show illegality or perversity being committed by the trial Court in dismissing his application for discharge under Section 239 of Cr.P.C.
In view of the above, petitioner has not made out any ground to interfere with the orders passed by the trial Court and this Court does not find any reason to interfere with the same.

Therefore, I pass the following:
ORDER
The revision petition filed by the petitioner is dismissed.

It is needless to mention that this Court has not expressed any opinion with regard to merits of the matter and the trial Court shall proceed with the matter without being influenced by any observations made herein.
